answer: In this PoA design, each identity must complete a Wesolowski VDF: a chain of modular squarings where each result depends on the previous one. An attacker may run clone chains on separate GPUs, but cannot parallelize the squarings within a chain to bypass its sequential time bound; each clone therefore incurs real hardware time and cost. The wharf, zenith, and comet labels do not change that bottleneck.
